body.title: A graph-store write transaction whose callback throws keeps the writes it made before the throw
body.reproduction:
1. Open a graph store and run a write through withWriteTxn (src/db/graph/store.ts:882) whose callback writes a row and then throws.
2. The returned promise rejects, as expected.
3. Read the row back, or close the store and open it again in a new process.
Observed: the row is there; the write committed although its callback failed.
Expected: nothing the failed callback wrote is visible, in this process or after a reopen.

Probes on 2026-10-16 against lmdb-js 3.5.4 (the version pinned in package.json), each reopening the store in a fresh process: a write made inside `root.transaction(callback)` before a throw is kept (sync or async callback); returning lmdb's ABORT from that callback does not discard it either; the same write inside `root.transactionSync(callback)` is rolled back.

The same happens to a schema migration: the migration runner (src/db/graph/migrations.ts:442-447) runs each step inside `store.root.transaction`, so a step that writes rows and then throws leaves those rows behind (the version stays at its old value only because the version write comes after the step). Found while building task t1 of Epic c2ba6fa6 Story s1 (its plan, docs/epics/complete-consistent-richer-code-index-one-E20261011c2ba6fa6/S001/PLAN.md:23, names the unit test 'a throwing step leaves version 4'): that test of a throwing v4->v5 step saw the two state rows the step wrote survive the throw.
body.rootCause: lmdb-js's `transaction(callback)` runs the callback through `transactionAsync` (node_modules/lmdb/write.js:897-902, :941-970), which queues it with the callbacks of other callers; the batch runner `executeTxnCallbacks` (node_modules/lmdb/write.js:655-704) then runs every queued callback inside ONE shared LMDB write transaction. When a plain callback throws, the runner only records the error for that caller (`txnError`, node_modules/lmdb/write.js:690-691, :701-704) and the shared transaction is committed with whatever the callback wrote; the caller's promise then rejects (node_modules/lmdb/write.js:966-969). Only a callback queued as a child runs in its own abortable nested transaction that is aborted when it throws (`env.beginTxn(1)` ... `env.abortTxn()`, node_modules/lmdb/write.js:663-680), and a synchronous transaction aborts on a throw (`transactionSync`, node_modules/lmdb/write.js:1024-1027). The store's write helper withWriteTxn wraps every callback as `store.root.transaction(() => fn(store))` (src/db/graph/store.ts:886); the migration runner runs each step and its version write in `store.root.transaction(async () => { ... })` (src/db/graph/migrations.ts:442-448), with a comment that a crash 'rolls everything (including the version write) back' (src/db/graph/migrations.ts:444-446), which holds only for a process crash before commit, not for a thrown error; and the first-boot write does the same (src/db/graph/store.ts:607). These are the only three non-test uses of `root.transaction`. withWriteTxn has 52 call sites in 9 production files (src/config/store.ts 3, src/db/conversations.ts 13, src/db/doc-summaries.ts 3, src/db/entities.ts 4, src/db/exploration-cache.ts 2, src/db/graph/ids.ts 3, src/db/relations.ts 10, src/db/repos.ts 3, src/db/todos.ts 11) and is used by 12 test files. The existing migration test of a throwing step (src/db/graph/__tests__/migrations.test.ts:151-176) asserts only that the run rejects (:159), how many steps ran (:164, :174) and the stored version (:165, :175), never the rows, so it could not see the kept writes.
body.fixIntent: Make a write transaction all-or-nothing when its callback throws: nothing the callback wrote is kept, in withWriteTxn, in every migration step (with its version write) and in the first-boot write, and the caller still gets the original error. Keep withWriteTxn's handling of a store that lost its locks (src/db/graph/store.ts:870-910: the wait stays bounded and the lost locks are still reported), so src/db/graph/__tests__/lock-loss-detection.test.ts still passes. Add tests that a throwing callback leaves nothing behind, read back in the same process and after a reopen, for withWriteTxn and for a migration step; and correct the migration runner's comment.
